ground_truth.location: Table 4, International terrorist attack (All countries, attacks with more than 15 deaths)
ground_truth.context: Table 4 ("Effect of Terrorist Attacks on Executive Approval Ratings").  Linear regression on time-series cross-sectional data of country-quarters: the percentage of the public approving of the executive in the quarter following the attack, regressed on an indicator for a major international terrorist attack (an attack with an international component under the Global Terrorism Database's definition and more than 15 deaths), the presence of a woman executive, their interaction, and controls for GDP growth, logged inflation, the left-center-right placement of the leader and elections, with country fixed effects and panel-corrected standard errors.  Sample: countries in the executive approval database that also appear in the Global Terrorism Database, 1975-2017.  This coefficient is the attack effect for men executives (the rally).

ground_truth.location: Table 4, International terrorist attack x Woman executive
ground_truth.context: Table 4, the paper's global test of the gender-revised rally framework: the coefficient on the interaction of a major international terrorist attack (more than 15 deaths) with a woman executive, in the same linear country-quarter regression of next-quarter executive approval (controls for woman executive, GDP, logged inflation, left-center-right placement of the leader and elections; country fixed effects; panel-corrected standard errors). Negative and significant at the 5% level in the paper.

i4r.notes: Coding error fixed: the election-quarter covariates (current quarter and four lags).  DP41 Table 1 Panel A col 6 / meta-database row "Fixing election quarter coding errors": -3.452 (SE 1.821), p = 0.058, N = 4,429 — no longer significant at 5%.  DP41 re-coded elections from public sources (60 contemporaneous observations changed; 317 amendments across the lags: US elections missing, Japan's upper house missing, run-offs and multi-round elections coded in one quarter only, errors for Austria 2016q4, Ecuador 1997q4, Iceland 2008q2/2012q2, Mexico 1991q3, Paraguay 2000q3, Turkey 2014q3).  Other DP41 variants (robustness, not corrections): no election controls -2.992 (1.841); no controls -2.650 (1.812); excluding the May-Manchester quarter -3.279 (1.982), and with corrected elections too -2.390 (1.945); country-clustered xtreg -3.194 (p = 0.558).  Authors' corrigendum (updated data, 14+ deaths threshold): -3.910 (1.798), N = 4,612.

ground_truth.context: Number of country-quarter observations in the Table 4 regression (all countries, attacks with more than 15 deaths).

i4r.notes: DP41 Table 1 Panel A col 6 (corrected election-quarter variables): the printed 4,328 becomes 4,429, because the re-coded election lags fill quarters that were missing (elections before a country's first observed quarter were coded by hand: 26 elections in 22 countries).  The corrigendum's re-built panel has 4,612.

ground_truth.location: Table 2, column May likeability, Manchester attack * time
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("Difference-in-Difference, with Fixed Effects"), May likeability column.  British Election Study internet panel, using waves before and after the 22 May 2017 Manchester Arena bombing. Outcome: how much the respondent likes Theresa May, 0 (strongly dislike) to 10 (strongly like).  Regressors: Manchester attack (the respondent was surveyed after the attack in the attack wave, wave 12), time (0 for waves before the attack, 1 for waves from 12 onward), their interaction (the coefficient here), wave fixed effects, and controls for identifying as ethnically British, gender, Labour party membership, other party membership, income and ideology.  OLS according to the table note; standard errors in parentheses.

i4r.notes: DP41 Table B1 col 1: -0.1274 (0.0187), N = 143,499, reproduced exactly; DP41 corrects nothing in the likeability model.  (The authors' 2024 corrigendum later restricts it to waves 9-12: -0.3273 (0.0255), N = 79,619.)

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=-0.099607 vs claimed=-0.1274 (relative error 21.82%, tolerance 14.68%, the ±1·SE band with SE=0.0187).

ground_truth.context: Table 2, May best PM column: the same difference-in-differences specification (Manchester attack, time, their interaction, wave fixed effects, full controls) with the outcome "Who would make the best prime minister?", coded 1 for Theresa May and 0 for Jeremy Corbyn.  The table note describes this column as a logistic regression; standard errors in parentheses.  This is the interaction coefficient.

i4r.notes: Coding error fixed: the best-PM outcome in waves 7-8 (35,060 of the 97,155 observations), where the question named David Cameron, is coded as preferring May.  DP41 Table B1 col 3 drops waves 1-8: -0.0502 (SE 0.0038), N = 62,095 — the coefficient barely moves. Fixing the estimator as well (logit, as the paper states, instead of the xtreg actually run) gives -0.6806 (0.0576) on all waves (col 4) and -1.0181 (0.0797) without waves 1-8 (col 5), on the log-odds scale. cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Table 4: N is 4486 country-quarters (44 countries) rather than the paper's 4328 (66 countries); the posted global_approval.dta contains 44 usable countries and no lead/lag or growth-rate variant tried (exploratory attempts 4 and 6) reproduced 4328.

Table 4: the dependent variable is the posted 'lag_approval' (the only approval series in the file), regressed on the contemporaneous 16+-death international attack indicator kill_16; GDP enters in levels (variable 'growth', rescaled by 1e6), execrlc linear. Coefficients are OLS with country dummies; panel-corrected SEs computed by hand (Beck-Katz, pairwise covariances), no AR(1) correction.

Table 2: both columns estimated by OLS (the May best PM column as a linear probability model, since the reported coefficients/SEs are on the probability scale despite the note saying logistic). Wave dummies entered after 'time' so the last collinear wave dummy is omitted, Stata-style; SEs clustered by respondent (not scored). Ideology uses ideology2 (missing set to midpoint), which reproduces both reported Ns exactly.
cell.notes: Attempts 1-6 explored the data (readme docx text, variable structure, sample-size searches for Table 4). Attempt 7 crashed (singular X'X in the PCSE function because GDP is in levels) and was fixed by rescaling GDP. Attempt 8 was the first scored run; I compared it with check_attempt (feedback.txt): the Table 4 coefficients were within tolerance, but N(Table 4) and the May-likeability interaction and time coefficients, plus the best-PM time coefficient, were off. Attempts 9 (crashed from a bug in the exploratory script) and 10 explored Table 2 variants (alternative ideology codings, treatment2, which wave dummy gets omitted, adding a Conservative dummy). None was better justified by the paper, so the final run reruns the attempt-8 script unchanged; its output is identical to attempt 8. Remaining gaps: May-likeability DiD interaction -0.0996 vs -0.1274 and time -0.451 vs -0.501; Table 4 N 4486 vs 4328. No docker run hung. replication_files.do was not opened.
